chapter: Owls, Werlein's and the OK record
title: Dr. Souchon's letter and hanging his bass in the museum
summary: Tape three: Brownlee wants to hang his old string bass in the jazz museum and talks about the letter and the museum's holdings.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: Norman Brownlee, Rio 4, May 5, 1961. And Ms. Brownlee has joined us so she can remind us.
I need reminding. I need two minds.
You wanted to say something about your bass.

Yes, I wanted to tell you about a very fine letter that I got from Dr. Sushon. With reference to my old days around the jazz fields in New Orleans. I happened to have been hospitalized when this letter came. And thus a delay in answering his lovely letter. And I wanted him to know that I thought that if they had room for it, I'd hang my old string bass up in the museum.
And I'm sure they'll find room.

They'll probably have rotating exhibits is probably what they'll do. Change them from month to month. I don't know what they're planning. I see. I don't know if you can talk to Harry about it. But I know they have so much stuff. They have Jack Lane's bass drum.

They have Jack, yes. And they have Rap's clarinet too. Rapola's clarinet. He tells me a lot of this in the letter. Which was the most interesting letter to me. And I certainly have to answer his letter. And I imagine qualify for my subscription to the magazine. Well, that's good.
You're going to get that they have good articles.
